violations.where: Account Line lifecycle (states imported/flagged/unmapped/mapped) vs Import Staging Row model & R-6
violations.why: The data model and R-6 state emphatically that unresolved/invalid rows are held as Import Staging Rows and 'no Account Line is created for it until it is mapped'; a 'category-less Account Line can never exist'. But the Account Line lifecycle starts in `imported` and transits through `flagged` and `unmapped` states (and `mapped → unmapped`), which models Account Lines existing before mapping and without a category — the opposite of R6's implementation.
violations.fix_hint: Delete the imported/flagged/unmapped states from the Account Line lifecycle; those belong to Import Staging Row. Account Line should begin at `mapped`.

violations.where: Dashboard View lifecycle 'Who' column vs permissions matrix and S-21
violations.why: The permissions matrix grants Bookkeeper ✓*(4) for Open/Save Dashboard View, and S-21 says 'Given the Bookkeeper has saved a Dashboard View'. But the Dashboard View lifecycle lists only 'Owner' as the actor for draft→saved, saved→archived, and archived→saved, denying the Bookkeeper a capability the matrix and a scenario grant.
violations.fix_hint: Change the Dashboard View lifecycle 'Who' to 'view owner (Owner or Bookkeeper)' to match the matrix/scenario, or restrict the matrix.

violations.where: Permissions matrix row 'Restore an archived record' (Bookkeeper ✓) applied to the User entity (which has archived_by/archived_at)
violations.why: R-9 restricts all user-account management to the Owner ('Bookkeepers, Managers, and Accountants cannot manage user accounts'). Yet the matrix grants Bookkeeper an unqualified '✓' to Restore an archived record, and User is a soft-deletable record. A Bookkeeper restoring an archived User account would be managing an account, contradicting R9.
violations.fix_hint: Scope the 'Restore an archived record' permission to exclude User records for the Bookkeeper, or make User restore Owner-only.

violations.where: R-12 delete guard vs R-4 edit lock / Account Line 'Edit lock'
violations.why: R-12 lets a Category be archived only after its Account Lines are 'reassigned to another Category or removed'. R-4 (and the Account Line Edit lock) forbid editing OR archiving any Account Line whose period is `closed`. If a Category's only lines live in closed periods, R-12's mandatory escape (reassign/remove those lines) is exactly what R-4 prohibits, so the Category can never be archived without first reopening a closed period — R-12's escape hatch is R-4's prohibition.
violations.fix_hint: State that R-12's delete guard ignores lines in closed periods, or require the Owner to reopen before reassigning; make the interaction explicit.

violations.where: R-12 Verify: 'reassign or archive those lines, retry → succeeds'
violations.why: R-12's verification test instructs the tester to reassign or archive the referencing Account Lines, but if those lines belong to a closed Period R-4 forbids that step, so the test cannot be executed for such a Category.
violations.fix_hint: Qualify the test to open-period lines, or add a reopen step.

violations.where: Dashboard View ownership note / R-20 vs cited decision d:record_ownership ('admins see all')
violations.why: R-20 and the visibility prose say saved Dashboard Views are visible only to their owner and 'the Owner is not exempt', while the cited decision record_ownership states 'admins see all'. The spec contradicts the very decision it cites as source.
violations.fix_hint: Cite a different rationale (personal views) rather than d:record_ownership, or reconcile the 'admins see all' language.

omissions.why: The Sheet action a9 has the Bookkeeper reopening a period, but the spec makes reopen Owner-only (justified by r4/approval_workflow). The action as literally stated in the Sheet is not implemented for the Bookkeeper; this is a deliberate narrowing that should be flagged.

omissions.item: record_duplicates (warn about likely duplicates and offer to merge)
omissions.why: The resolved-ish decision to warn about likely duplicates and offer to merge is not implemented; the spec only enforces hard uniqueness (email, period label) and case-insensitive category matching, with no duplicate-warning or merge feature.

scope_creep.item: A Manager may view and export only Expense Figures whose Category is one of that Manager's allowed_areas; Revenue Figures, Profit Summary, and company-wide totals are hidden.
Every upload, mapping, correction, and period close/reopen writes an AuditEntry capturing the acting User and timestamp; AuditEntry rows can be created but never edited or deleted.
Every User has a role, and every User whose role is Manager has at least one allowed area assigned at invitation time.
Only the Owner may reopen a closed Period, acting as the single approver, overriding any example that showed another actor reopening; the reopen writes an AuditEntry.
Import Staging Rows that are unmapped or validation-failed never contribute to any figure; an irreparable flagged row may be discarded by the Owner or Bookkeeper to unblock the Period.

Account Lines store positive amounts for ordinary income/expense entries and negative amounts for refunds/credits; totals sum signed amounts within their type so refunds and credits reduce the relevant total.
Deletion is soft everywhere: a deleted record sets archived_at and archived_by and can be restored; there is no hard delete and no automatic purge in v1.
When two editors save the same record, the later updated_at write wins; the app does not lock or merge.
A saved Dashboard View is visible only to the User named in its owner field; no other actor, including the Owner, may open or save another user's View.
Import staging rows are not Account Lines and are never counted in any figure.
The Account Line type must match its Category's type.
An Account Line is only ever created from a staging row after a Category is assigned.
The uploaded file itself is retained after import (never discarded) to support rollback.
email is unique across all users.
Owner|assign role and allowed areas to|User
Does not host multiple separate businesses with partitioned data; all records live in one shared pool for the single business.
Does not let anyone define their own roles or per-record permission sets; the four roles and their fixed powers are built in.
Does not work offline or sync later; it is an online-only browser application.
Does not detect foreign currencies on import or convert amounts; every file is assumed to already use the org's one configured currency.
Does not auto-remove records after any retention window; records are kept until an actor archives them via restorable soft delete.
Does not let admins add custom fields, build their own reports, or configure automation that acts on records automatically.
Does not expose a full data export or an API; the only way out is downloading figure lists as CSV subject to view permissions.
There is no undo action in v1.

missing.item: Only the Owner and Bookkeeper may upload or edit spreadsheets and figures; Managers and Accountants can only view.
A Manager may only see figures for the areas assigned to them, not the whole company.

R-8 — Re-uploading a Period replaces its figures
R-9 — Only the Owner manages users and access
R-10 — Every mutation is recorded in an unalterable history
R-11 — Users carry role and allowed areas
R-12 — A Category in use cannot be archived
R-13 — An upload needs file, period, and uploader
R-14 — Period labels are unique
R-15 — Unmapped and validation-failed rows are staged
R-16 — Signed-amount aggregation
R-17 — Only the Owner reopens a closed Period
R-18 — Deletion is soft and restorable
R-19 — Concurrent edits resolve last-write-wins
R-20 — Saved Dashboard Views are personal
